conceptZh: 都：全部、通通；玩具戰士把一排彈珠都打光，每彈一下就落下一筆。
object: a chunky toy warrior with a foam sword and round shield, and a swarm of bouncy colored rubber balls that ricochet around the frame
morph: every rubber ball that bounces off his shield drops one stroke of 都 into place, until all of them are used
creativeAngle: 玩具戰士想把所有的球都擋下來，卻只會亂揮泡棉劍；每顆球彈到盾牌或牆上，就落下一筆，所有球都用完字就完成了。
promptEn: An 8-second bright, clean toy-animation clip on a solid pale powder-blue backdrop. Cast: a chunky toy warrior with a foam sword and a round shield, all bravado and very little skill, and a bag of bouncy rubber balls in red, yellow, green and blue that spill out and ricochet on their own. The only text on screen is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 都, drawn in saturated crimson strokes, ending centered, uncropped, about 70 percent of frame height with margins. 0.0-1.5s: the warrior stomps in, plants his shield, swings his foam sword in a big arc to show he will block everything, and trips over the open bag; five rubber balls pop out and bounce off the floor. The first narrated 都 lands as the red ball hits the shield with a bonk and drops one crimson stroke into the air. 1.5-3.5s: balls ricochet off the walls, the warrior's helmet and the underside of his shield, boing, boing, boing; he turns left, then right, then spins in a full circle swinging blindly, and each ricochet that connects drops one more stroke into place while the others bounce on. The second narrated 都 lands as the yellow ball clips his sword tip and drops the final stroke, completing 都. 3.5-5.0s: the warrior lifts his shield high and every remaining ball rolls into it and stops, all the colors nested like a bowl of candy; he stares at it in wide-eyed joy, and the shield sinks under the weight. As the word 都是 is spoken, the warrior points at each ball one after another, and all the balls give a small hop together, as if to say they are all his. 5.0-8.0s: the glyph is perfectly still and readable for the last 3 seconds while the warrior, to one side, juggles two balls on his sword tip and does a small happy shield dance and the other balls bounce gently in place. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks slowly and distinctly in clear Taiwanese Mandarin, clear tones, no erhua, reading exactly these syllables: 都、都、都是 (ㄉㄡ、ㄉㄡ、ㄉㄡ ㄕˋ). The character twice with a short pause, then the word once, then stop. The word is audio only. No background music, no extra speech, no subtitles or flashing effects; stylized toys only, no real people.

conceptZh: 都：全部、通通。玩具海盜看見積木小隊疊成的高塔頂上有一枚金幣，鸚鵡偏偏停在他鼻子上遮住眼睛；他衝鋒撞歪一次，再衝一次「碰」撞上積木塔，被撞飛的積木全都掉下來排成「都」，海盜張開雙臂說：這些都是我的！
object: a tall wobbly tower of interlocking crimson building bricks with one gold coin balanced on top, far across the frame from a barrel-shaped toy pirate whose parrot keeps landing on his nose
morph: the pirate's full-speed BONK into the brick tower shakes every brick loose; the falling bricks click together mid-air into the left component 者 (a 土 top, the short diagonal, then a square 日 of bricks) and the right ear 阝, completing a solid crimson 都
creativeAngle: 全新「衝鋒撞牆」版本：主角換成玩具海盜，笑點來自不合作的鸚鵡每次都停在最糟的位置（鼻子、眼罩、金幣上），害他第一次衝過頭、第二次才真正撞上積木塔；撞擊本身把積木震成「都」字，不再是物件安靜變形。詞語「都是」用海盜張開雙臂把整個字圈進懷裡的動作表現「全部都是我的」，聲音與畫面同一個故事。
promptEn: An 8-second bright, clean toy-animation clip on a solid pale sand-yellow backdrop, nothing busy behind. Cast: a barrel-shaped toy pirate with a navy coat, a wooden peg leg, a big black hat and a hook hand, all swagger and no steering; his small green toy parrot, who flatly refuses to cooperate and always lands on the worst possible spot; and a squad of interlocking crimson building bricks stacked as one tall wobbly tower at the far right of the frame with a single gold coin balanced on top. The only text on screen is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 都, built from saturated crimson bricks, ending centered, uncropped, about 70 percent of frame height with margins. 0.0-1.5s: the pirate stands at the far left, spots the gold coin on top of the brick tower, eyes go huge, and he points his hook straight at it; the parrot hops off his shoulder and lands squarely on his nose, covering one eye. He shoves the parrot aside, digs his peg leg into the floor and leans way back in a big wind-up. 1.5-3.0s: first try, he charges across the frame, but the parrot flaps right in front of his face, so he veers and barrels straight past the tower off the right edge with a whoosh, then stomps back into view and glares at the parrot. Bigger wind-up: he leans back so far his barrel body tips onto its rim, the parrot settles on top of his hat like a lookout, and the brick squad on the tower wobbles nervously. 3.0-4.5s: the big charge, full speed, straight into the brick tower, BONK, with a squashy cartoon flatten and a wobble; every brick pops into the air and the gold coin spins up and away. The first narrated 都 lands exactly on the crash as the loosened bricks begin dropping into place, clicking together into the left component 者 (a 土 top, the short diagonal, then a square 日 of bricks). The second narrated 都 lands as the last bricks snap into the right ear 阝 and the complete crimson 都 clicks solid and still. 4.5-5.5s: the pirate peels himself off the floor pancake-flat, pops back into barrel shape, and staggers to the lower left in a dizzy grin with little stars circling his hat; the gold coin bounces once and the parrot lands on it before he can grab it. 5.5-8.0s: the glyph 都 stays perfectly still and readable, never touched or covered. As the word 都是 is spoken, the pirate spreads both arms as wide as they go in one big sweep that takes in the whole glyph and the coin, as if to say these are all mine, and the parrot copies the pose with both wings spread. For the rest of the hold he does a tiny peg-leg victory hop and the parrot flaps from the coin to his nose one more time. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks slowly and distinctly in clear Taiwanese Mandarin, clear tones, no erhua, reading exactly these syllables: 都、都、都是 (ㄉㄡ、ㄉㄡ、ㄉㄡ ㄕˋ). The character twice with a short pause, then the word once, then stop. The word is audio only.
